''Paspalum fissifolium'' }} '''''Axonopus fissifolius''''' is a [[Poaceae|grass]] species which is often used as permanent [[pasture]]. Common names include '''common carpetgrass''',{{PLANTS|id=AXFI|taxon=Axonopus fissifolius|accessdate=9 January 2016}} '''caratao grass''', and '''Louisiana grass''' in the United States, and '''mat grass''', '''narrow-leaved carpet grass''', and '''Durrington grass''' in Australia. == Description == The leaf blades of ''A. fissifolius'' may be either folded or flat, and have find hairs along the margin. They may become purple or reddish in color when mature.Magee, P. (2005). ''Plant Fact Sheet: Common Carpetgrass Axonopus fissifolius''. N.R.C.S. United States Department of Agriculture. Baton Rouge, LA. == Distribution and habitat == This species' native range encompasses the southeastern United States (from Virginia westward to Texas), Grenada in the Caribbean, and throughout Central and South America. It has been introduced to regions within Asia, Africa, Australia and the Pacific Islands.{{Cite web |title=Axonopus fissifolius - Tropical Forages |url=https://tropicalforages.info/text/entities/axonopus_fissifolius.htm |access-date=2025-08-06 |website=tropicalforages.info}} ''A. fissifolius'' may be found in habitat types such as sandy forests, pine flatwoods. and grassland environments (specifically those with poor drainage).Weakley, A.
